observations: Unmodified ANGEL source passage starts at raw index 249 / measure 137. Query and indexed source durations both equal [0.5,0.5,0.5,0.5,1,0.5].

The only captured scoring path uses index 232 / measure 131, same transposed intervals but durations [1,0.5,0.5,0.5,0.5,1]. Interval score 100, rhythm 71.25. Expected source absent among 82 exact plus 18 similar results.
cases.diagnosis: A different rhythmic occurrence was selected for scoring despite the exact source passage existing. Candidate-window selection and result truncation need investigation; original query itself is not changed.
cases.proposal: Compare multiple same-interval occurrences using full rhythm before choosing a representative; preserve source window provenance and test repeated-motif counterexamples.

observations: Expected source ranks 38. Top 10 labeled Exact all pass the independent pitch, onset and duration audit under one transposition and tempo scale.
cases.diagnosis: Seven-note simplified query genuinely matches other passages more exactly under these comparison dimensions. Lower source rank alone is not a scoring defect.
cases.proposal: Prefer asking for a longer distinctive continuation over forcing the original source above genuine exact matches.

observations: Expected source ranks 74. Top three Exact labels have maximum duration differences of 0.25 query beat after median tempo normalization; first two also have 0.25-beat onset differences.
cases.diagnosis: Default Exact labeling can conceal material rhythmic differences, consistent with the previously deferred strict-exact issue. This audit is not a full exact-option regression or human relevance judgment.
cases.proposal: Separate tolerant rhythm retrieval from explicit duration/rest exact classification, then reassess ranking without work-specific boosts.

observations: UN DI, FELICE expected stream: inHits=true, inCandidates=false; no scored paths or rejection events for that stream. Expected source absent from returned results.
cases.diagnosis: Expected stream disappears between initial hits and alignment candidates, unlike a final similarity-score rejection.
cases.proposal: Audit short-query candidate truncation and retained anchor/offset diversity; compare cost and negative controls before expansion.

observations: Expected melody source ranks 33 at score 97; ranks 1–3 are the 13 JOURS EN FRANCE Piano Solo, Violin and Piano Duet, and Trio sources at score 100.
The work is visible at the top through alternate arrangements. Source-file Top10 failure must not be reported as work retrieval failure.
cases.diagnosis: Expected-file rank and confirmed alternate-arrangement retrieval differ.
cases.proposal: Retain separate source-file and reviewed work-level outcomes; do not force the exact source ahead of other valid arrangements.

observations: Expected source file ranks 4; ranks 1–3 all have title 13 JOURS EN FRANCE and are Piano Solo, Violin and Piano Duet, Violin/Cello/Piano Trio sources.
Rank 1–3 have reported score 100; expected source score 97.
cases.diagnosis: Source-file rank 4 does not mean the work disappeared; alternative arrangements occupy preceding ranks. This is not evidence of incorrect ranking.
cases.proposal: Keep source-file recall separate from analyst-confirmed work identity; do not force the original source to rank first.

observations: Expected source 2 Become 1 enters hits and candidates, but all 5 traced paths are rejected by low-information-floors.
Two scored paths reach local 93.0769, pitch 97.4545, interval 97.3018, rhythm 100 and coverage 1. Their equality score is 85.4545 and meter score 10.9091.
Current low-information floors require equality >=88 and meter >=60, among other conditions; these traced paths fail both. Deletion removes 0.25 beat, shifting subsequent query onsets.
cases.diagnosis: Candidate recall succeeds but low-information admission rejects high melodic similarity. Arrival-phase shift, repetitive pitch alignment and admission policy require joint review; not a simple missing candidate.
cases.proposal: Evaluate onset-phase consistency and competing ornament-omission paths for repetitive queries; retain strict negative controls and do not globally lower the floors.

cases.diagnosis: Source retrieved but some query attacks remain unmatched.
cases.proposal: Check which changed/retained notes were excluded, separately from successful work retrieval.

cases.diagnosis: Expected stream entered scoring and has low-information-floor rejection evidence. Other traced rejections may also apply.
cases.proposal: Compare deletion-induced onset shifts and strict metrical/equality floors using repetitive-query negative controls; do not globally relax admission.
